chapter: Technique and the Covington band's sound
title: A stable six-piece band, repertoire and white dances
summary: The band never changed personnel; they played blues and old numbers like Tiger Rag, mostly white dances at the hotel and Romeo Park ball games.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: That's correct. Yeah. Had all of you been together most of this time? All the time. That's the whole bunch right there. That's the whole bunch. You didn't have any changes back and forth from one to the other.
No, no. That's the whole bunch right there. Because we liked it one another and we liked what we was doing. We just had to start playing together and we liked it.
Can you remember what type of pieces you played? Did you play like for instance many blues or the

late popular songs? No, no. What did you play? It wasn't like that. We played the blues all right. And some of them late ones come out there but say like them old time, It's A Plenty, you know what I mean? Yeah. Well Tiger Rag, we didn't play Tiger Rag much but when the people come ask for it we'd play it. Because this guy here used to like to make that Tiger, you know what I mean? So we'd play it out there unless somebody come and ask for Tiger Rag, we played the Tiger Rag. And did you play mostly for
white dances over there at the hotel or not? Yeah, mostly white dances. Not many colored dances over

there on that side. No, no. We didn't have too many, but we played for them though. He did play some of them. Yeah, because they had a place out in Covenant they called it Romeo Park. See they had a dance hall. You heard about the Romeo? No, I don't know about that. Well they had a park there where the boys used to play ball and we used to play for the ball games and sometimes we'd give the dance right after the ball game like that while we'd play the dance for them like that.
